findings.message: Adding `(.result_contract == 2) and` does not fix a tautology when the baseline artifact already emits result_contract:2 — both halves of the `and` are true at baseline, so NEGCTL still passes; the acceptance-gate confirms all nine SPEC assertions (SPEC-1/2/5/6/7/8/11) remain tautological after this change.

SPEC-7 is explicitly listed as tautological by the acceptance-gate but is not touched in this diff — it still uses bare `has('exit_code')` without any result_contract guard, so it passes on a v1 result that happens to expose exit_code at top level.

SPEC-8 pipe-delimits `_spec8_term` (signal-death mapping) with `_spec8_rc2` (jq boolean from OUT_JSON_3); if jq fails or OUT_JSON_3 is absent, `_spec8_rc2` silently collapses to empty string via `2>/dev/null`, producing composite `'interrupted|'` that matches nothing rather than failing with a clear diagnostic.

The combined jq boolean `(.result_contract == 2) and has('field')` returns a single true/false that cannot distinguish 'wrong contract version' from 'required field absent', so any assertion failure is opaque about which invariant broke.

SPEC-11 in the fallback-writer test now asserts `(.result_contract == 2) and (.run_mode == 'full')`; if the baseline implementation already writes result_contract:2 and run_mode:full (consistent with the acceptance-gate NEGCTL FAIL), this assertion is also tautological and does not guard the v2 contract shape it claims to verify.
